segments.text: Your vagina has a microbiome too, but it's unique. In the gut, more diversity is better, but in the vagina, a single species is healthier, and diversity is actually the warning. [music] Lots of things affect the microbiome. Menstruation, sex, semen, antibiotics, and hormones. And an unhealthy vaginal microbiome has huge effects. It's associated with higher risk [music] of pre-term birth, higher risk of acquiring HIV, and even lower IVF success. But most bacterial vaginosis is [music] asymptomatic, so a lot of women are actually in that state without even knowing it. What's obvious is that we
